summary: Iteration 4 targeted verification of the freshly-regenerated rock.png and flower_yellow.png PNG assets. Both assets are visually clean: rock.png is a plain grey cel-shaded pebble with a single glossy upper-left highlight and NO cartoon face (no eyes, no pupils, no mouth); flower_yellow.png shows 3 yellow daisies with solid orange centers, green stems and leaves, and NO baked-in faces on the flower centers. When rendered in the live Phaser/WebGL scene, both assets appear crisp with no visible checkerboard or dashed-noise artifacts in their transparent backgrounds. Menu freeze from iteration 3 is preserved: pixel-diff between two menu screenshots taken 2.5s apart shows only 0.5% of pixels changed, and the diff mask is exclusively (a) thin diagonal rain streaks scattered across the whole scene, and (b) the walking corgi silhouette near the ground line; all parallax layers, the CORGI HOP logo, the 'Tap PLAY to start hopping!' hint, trees, bushes, rocks and flowers are pixel-identical. Rain particles are clearly visible as falling white streaks over the menu. PLAY regression works: tapping the PLAY button opens GameScene, HUDScene mounts (score '0', BEST:0 trophy, bone counter, pause button, TAP TO JUMP paw prompt), and gameplay parallax scrolls in real-time (clouds shift, a fence obstacle spawns and scrolls in, a collectible bone spawns). SHOP button regression also confirmed (an early errant tap opened the ShopScene with Remove Ads / Starter Pack / Premium Corgi / All Corgis / FREE +25 TREATS + WATCH + RESTORE + BACK all rendering correctly). No JS console errors were observed on any screen; only the permissible Chromium GL_CLOSE_PATH_NV WebGL driver performance warnings appeared. The ?/P/menu-corgis-button taps in this run did not visibly trigger scene changes at the coordinates I tried, but these were verified working in iteration 3 and no source changed for them; likely a tap-coordinate miss rather than a regression.

critical_code_review_comments: The regenerated PNGs contain non-zero RGB values in alpha=0 pixels (visible in Chrome DevTools transparency-preview checkerboard view). This is cosmetically fine because Phaser/WebGL correctly ignores alpha=0 pixels during rendering, but any future tool that reads raw RGB (e.g., custom shader without proper premultiply) would surface the artifacts. Consider running an extra `Image.paste(bg=(0,0,0,0))` mask pass in scripts/regen_clean_props.py to zero out RGB where alpha==0.

The HowToPlay `?` and Privacy `P` icons are stacked in the top-right around page x=350; try y=210 for ? and y=260 for P. All click hits go through Phaser's input system via mousedown+up so page.mouse.click works. Backend/API tests were not requested.
